Container.Name: backup-engine
Container.Overview:
Off-site, encrypted AWS S3 backups for Unraid: define backup jobs — versioned via restic, archive via rclone (e.g. Glacier Deep Archive), or versioned-files (per-file version history via rclone + a SQLite catalog, on any storage class including Deep Archive) — for any folder under one read-only source mount. The off-site leg of a 3-2-1 strategy.
Before starting this container, provision an AWS destination (bucket + least-privilege IAM user) with the included OpenTofu module or the scripted `setup.sh` — see the README — then populate backup.env / secrets.env under the Config path below, and create backup jobs (versioned via restic / archive via rclone / versioned-files) in the GUI → Jobs.
The GUI's Cost estimate page shows a job-aware view of what you're spending — real bucket usage priced at live AWS rates (no credentials needed), a per-job breakdown, and a live what-if — plus an optional connection to AWS Cost Explorer for the true invoice/forecast, via a separate, read-only credential you enter on that page (never the runtime backup key).
Container.Config: Parent of everything you might back up (read-only). Create backup jobs in the GUI → Jobs.

Where restore / download / warm-up / test-restore WRITE recovered files. Deliberately a SEPARATE, read-write mount from the read-only Source root above, so a restore can never overwrite what it protects — recovered files land outside the backed-up tree. Keep it out from under a folder you back up.
Host path of the restore mount, shown in the GUI and used to validate a typed restore target. Match it to the left-hand side of the Restore target mapping above.
